Packaging claim: A Fire Sprinkler Waits for Heat, Not Smoke
Core fact: In a glass-bulb sprinkler, heat expands liquid in the bulb until it shatters at its rated temperature.
Second reveal: The broken bulb releases that sprinkler head so water can flow; typical home systems activate the head nearest the fire.
First frame: show a close-up of a sprinkler bulb warming and releasing water immediately, large and recognizable. Animate the physical change or causal chain without invented labels or unsupported details. Tell points or reacts without covering the object.
Fact boundaries: Do not claim smoke alone trips a heat-operated head or that every head sprays at once; avoid showing a live safety test.
